body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{fold}}\), characterize the joint limit of learned endpoint marks, their compensator, and the feasible convex argmin when \(nJ_n^{-(\alpha_a+1)}\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\). Determine necessary and sufficient primitive conditions for an infinitely divisible limit, a Cox mixture, or a more general fold-coupled Poisson functional.
body.justification: Order-one training-fold boundary information can couple evaluation marks despite cross-fitting.
body.gap: The located work has oracle weights, regular likelihood scores, or scalar stable sums, not a fold-labelled critical boundary experiment.
body.consumer: A solution would support aggressive propensity adaptation outside the subcritical preservation window.

obligation.what_is_open: Classify the critical fold-labelled Poisson functional into infinitely divisible, Cox, and genuinely fold-coupled cases using primitive conditions.
obligation.obstruction: The handle does not specify the limiting constrained-likelihood map or compensator. Different measurable maps compatible with it produce each of the three requested classes, so no necessary-and-sufficient classification follows from the frozen core.
obligation.attempted: Reduced every possible subsequential critical law to a measurable fold-labelled Poisson functional and isolated the shared-training inputs that prevent independent marking.
obligation.partial_result:
At critical resolution, let \(N_1,\ldots,N_K\) denote the fold-labelled endpoint Poisson limits.  Any subsequential limit allowed by the handle must have the measurable form
\[
\mathcal S
=\sum_{k=1}^K
\left[
\int \Phi_k\!\left(z,y;\,
\mathcal L_k(N_1,\ldots,N_{k-1},N_{k+1},\ldots,N_K)\right)dN_k(z,y)
-\mathcal C_k(N_1,\ldots,N_K)
\right],
\]
followed by the positive-curvature quantile argmin map.  Here \(\mathcal L_k\) is the limiting constrained-likelihood map trained off fold \(k\), and \(\mathcal C_k\) is its compensator.  This representation follows from foldwise cross-fitting and the definition of \(\mathfrak H_{\rm fold}\).

The frozen primitives do not specify the maps \(\mathcal L_k\), their boundary constraint geometry, or convergence of the compensators.  Because \(\mathcal L_k\) and \(\mathcal L_{k'}\) share Poisson inputs, the marks need not be independently marked.  A deterministic \(\mathcal L_k\) gives an ordinary infinitely divisible Poisson integral; an exogenous random intensity can give a Cox mixture; and a shared fold functional can give a law that is neither.  All three behaviors are compatible with the stated handle.  Therefore no necessary-and-sufficient primitive classification can be derived until the critical constrained-likelihood map and its compensator convergence are specified.
